chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Ishaq, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who bought a female slave and said to her, 'I will come to you with the price.' He said, 'If he comes within the time between them and a month, then the sale is valid; otherwise, there is no sale for him.'

key_terms.بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ شَهْرٍ: between them and a month (within a month)

ai.seo_question: What is the time limit for paying the price in a deferred sale of a slave according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes a specific temporal limit for deferred payment in slave sales, ruling that if the buyer fails to pay within one month, the transaction becomes void (*faskh*). This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on clarity and timeliness in financial contracts to prevent disputes arising from indefinite delays, distinguishing it from general sale principles where longer credit periods might be permissible.
